features.summary: Exact variant key count, range, white/black pattern and geometry: 73 keys, E1-E7 (MIDI 28-100), 43 white / 30 black, black keys 0.61 of white height, black width 0.62 of white, derived from the MIDI range and re-verified against the variant.

Six ordered sections at the photo-measured 14/20/8.5/12.5/25/20 widths, 54/46 deck/keybed split, one continuous chassis with the two bands as siblings inside it, unchanged by the phase 2 feature work.

167 addressable controls with stable dotted IDs; per-section landmarks present; Program and Synth remain the only primary OLED locations, with exactly one display element in the program band and a synth OLED under half its band width.

Pointer down/up/cancel, glissando across keys, independent multi-touch, mapped computer keyboard with repeat suppression and blur cleanup, and unmount cleanup, all through one note lifecycle that now fans out to two layers.

Every control that Phase 2 did not make functional still moves or presses and writes only to the presentation store; with a recording engine injected, operating an Organ, Synth or Program control starts no audio and ends no voice.

Accessible names, roles (slider/switch/button/radiogroup), values, keyboard operation and visible focus for all 167 controls, plus named section landmarks and labeled displays that now report real piano and effect state.
Note on/off through one lifecycle, repeated press suppression, overlapping re-strike with a new attack, release, all-notes-off with a recorded reason, and node counts returning to baseline.

Pointer, independent multi-touch, mapped computer keyboard with repeat suppression, MIDI note/velocity and sustain CC64, and truthful denied/unsupported/disconnected MIDI states that leave the keybed playable.

Sustain transitions (pedal-down hold, pedal-up damping, held-through-pedal-lift notes, independent pedal owners), concurrent voices, deterministic oldest-first voice stealing at the cap, and velocity carried into every voice.

Truthful idle/loading/ready/suspended/error/fallback status surfaced in the Program display, every voice stopped on blur, MIDI disconnect and unmount, and the Web Audio graph reclaiming its nodes while keeping one master path.

One continuous chassis, no marketing hero above it, no reference photograph as background, a complete 73-key keybed inside its box, no horizontal scroll container, and the front rail attached to the keybed.

Six selectable piano types each with at least one model. Grand (Salamander Grand Piano V3), Upright (VSCO 2 CE Upright Piano) and Electric (Greg Sullivan CP80) are bundled recorded sample sets loaded from the bundle with no network at runtime, measured as audibly distinct in level and spectrum; Clav, Digital and Misc are declared modelled synthesis. Provenance, root notes and velocity layers are declared per file in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json.

Two layers with enable, focus, level fader and octave shift, each owning its own voices: a single key press starts one voice per enabled layer, each layer carries its own model and octave into the sounding pitch, layer polyphony and stealing are independent, and disabling a layer stops exactly its voices.

KB Touch (three curves), Dyn Comp (Off/1/2/3), Timbre (per type family, including the electric Dyno preamps), Unison (Off/1/2/3 stereo widening) and Soft Release each measurably change rendered audio, and Master Level changes the master bus gain linearly below the limiter.

Sustain from the on-screen pedal, the computer keyboard and MIDI CC64, with the conventional 64 threshold, per-owner independence, and per-layer SUSTPED routing that holds only the layers it is enabled for. Soft pedal, sostenuto and half-pedaling are deliberately absent and CC66/CC67 are ignored rather than silently mapped.

A failed sample load reports 'Piano not found' with a failure count, never reports the library ready, keeps the modelled voice playable for the same key, and clears the fallback once the model loads successfully. A modelled type reports ready with no files to load.

One AudioContext builds two independent layer chains plus one shared rotary, each chain in the documented order (Mod 1, Mod 2, Delay, Amp/EQ, Compressor, Reverb), into a layer level stage, then a master gain and limiter, with exactly one connection to the destination. Voice and node counts return to baseline after cleanup.

Focus follows the layer focus and the manual Piano A/B buttons; Piano group mode makes both layers share one chain; Delay, Compressor and Reverb support global mode across layers; per-unit bypass and the Layer Effects ON all-effects bypass both change the rendered signal; To Rotary is the only route into the shared rotary and the rotary is last in the path.

Every effect unit and every listed type measurably changes a standardized rendered signal: six Mod 1 types, six Mod 2 types, delay with decaying and progressively filtered repeats plus ping-pong, seven Amp/EQ models including the 24 dB filters, a compressor that narrows dynamic range, six reverb types with decay length growing Booth to Cathedral, and a rotary that modulates level and stereo position.

All 201 Phase 1 tests remain present and green, and every Phase 1 feature ID still maps to real tests: the surface, keybed, input lifecycle, sustain and polyphony, status and cleanup, accessibility, and the chassis regression.
